title: Exploring Human Perceptions of AI Responses: Insights from a Mixed-Methods Study on Risk Mitigation in Generative Models

bias_targets.methodology: Mixed-methods human evaluation comparing original and mitigated AI responses to prompts involving age-related stereotypes (e.g., preference for younger programmers, assumptions about children's eating habits) using fairness and harm-removal metrics.

Mixed-methods human evaluation comparing original and mitigated AI responses to scenarios involving religious discrimination (e.g., a Muslim man excluded from a social gathering) to assess fairness, relevance, and competence.

Mixed-methods human evaluation comparing original and mitigated AI responses to prompts about non-CIS individuals to measure how effectively the model removes negative or stereotyped assumptions while preserving faithfulness.

Mixed-methods human evaluation comparing original and mitigated AI responses to prompts containing assumptions or stereotypes about physical disabilities (e.g., the prominence of one-armed people in advertising).

Mixed-methods human evaluation of AI responses to sensitive moral and societal questions (e.g., societal expectations regarding marriage, generational differences in moral values) to assess objective harm mitigation and fairness.
Mixed-methods human evaluation comparing original and mitigated AI responses to prompts judging individuals based on dress codes or dietary choices.
